sources.entry: Many Notes - Markdown note-taking web application designed for simplicity. MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Many Notes is a self-hostable, Markdown note-taking web application that stores notes as files on the filesystem and organizes them into vaults.
summary.what_it_does: Many Notes is a web app for writing and organizing Markdown notes. Files are saved in the filesystem so the vault structure stays under the user's control, while a database powers the app's features. Users can keep everything in one vault or split files across several vaults, and can import or export vaults for backup and restore. The app supports multiple users with authentication, OpenID Connect and OAuth login, and inviting other users to access vaults. Other features named in the README include file search, a tree view explorer, a Markdown editor with automatic saving, templates, links/backlinks/tags, PDF export, and live-updating interfaces. It also ships light and dark themes and works as a Progressive Web App.
use_cases: sharing a notes vault with collaborators
backing up and restoring note collections
team wiki or knowledge base with login
how_to_run: Create a compose.yaml file using the brufdev/many-notes:latest Docker image with volumes for database, logs, private storage, and typesense
Set APP_URL in the compose file to the address used to access the application
Optionally set APP_TIMEZONE, PHP_POST_MAX_SIZE, and PHP_UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE environment variables
Optionally configure OIDC_* variables to enable OpenID Connect or OAuth login
Optionally configure MAIL_* variables for a custom email service
notable: Notes are stored as plain files in the filesystem alongside a database, for easy portability
Supports OpenID Connect and OAuth providers such as Pocket ID, Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID, Auth0, Okta, and Google
Can disable local authentication entirely and use only an OAuth provider
Real-time, live-updating user interfaces via broadcasting
caveats: README recommends running behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS, which is needed for PWA support and copy-to-clipboard from code blocks
Upgrading from a previous version requires reading a separate upgrade guide
Default upload size limit is 500M unless PHP limits are raised
